analysis.evidence: The direct object אֶת עֵינָיו means “his eyes,” so Lot lifts his eyes to look. The next verb, וַיַּרְא (“and he saw”), introduces what he saw.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with Lot as its subject.
analysis.sense: lift the eyes to look up

evidence.note: The genealogy lists Abram and Haran among Terah’s sons and names Lot as Haran’s son.
וְלוֹט עִמּוֹ names Lot as a companion of Abram on the journey from Egypt.

article.name: לוֹט
article.summary: Lot was the son of Haran, Abram’s brother. He accompanied Abram from Egypt toward the Negeb. The meaning of his name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for לוֹט. The derivation of the name is uncertain.
draft.definition: Lot, son of Haran and nephew of Abram.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:27 names Haran as Lot’s father. Genesis 13:1 names Lot as Abram’s companion on the journey from Egypt.

analysis.evidence: וַיִּשָּׂא לוֹט אֶת עֵינָיו means “Lot lifted his eyes.” The following וַיַּרְא continues with the same subject as Lot sees the whole Jordan plain.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun without a prefix or suffix. Lot is the subject of both וַיִּשָּׂא and וַיַּרְא.
Hebrew direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: וַיִּשָּׂא לוֹט אֶת עֵינָיו means “Lot lifted his eyes.” The next verb, וַיַּרְא (“and he saw”), introduces what came into view, the whole Jordan plain.
analysis.morphology: Common noun of both genders in the dual construct, with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix referring to Lot.
analysis.sense: sight; eyes lifted up or opened to see

analysis.evidence: Lot lifts his eyes and surveys אֶת כָּל כִּכַּר הַיַּרְדֵּן, the whole Jordan plain. The following clause כִּי כֻלָּהּ מַשְׁקֶה describes what he saw about it: the entire plain was well watered.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces the Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with Lot as the subject.
Hebrew direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Lot sees אֶת כָּל כִּכַּר הַיַּרְדֵּן, “the whole Jordan plain.” The following כֻלָּהּ, “all of it,” confirms that he sees the plain in its entirety.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun governing כִּכַּר הַיַּרְדֵּן.

analysis.evidence: In כִּכַּר הַיַּרְדֵּן, “the plain of the Jordan,” the river gives the plain its name. Lot sees that the whole plain is well watered.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes the proper name and doubles its initial yod.

analysis.evidence: After וַיַּרְא, “he saw,” כִּי introduces what Lot saw about the Jordan plain: כֻלָּהּ מַשְׁקֶה, “all of it was well watered.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew conjunction with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: that (what is seen, known or said)

analysis.evidence: Lot sees כָּל כִּכַּר הַיַּרְדֵּן, the whole Jordan plain. The suffix in כֻלָּהּ refers back to כִּכַּר, and כִּי כֻלָּהּ מַשְׁקֶה says that all of it was well watered.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with a third-person feminine singular possessive suffix referring to the Jordan plain.
